carrier_invariant_or_forced_on_this_fixt: f0_diag_a0 and f0_coh_a0: both log2(16) = 4 by construction; cannot ever separate DIAG from COHERENT in this fixture family

f0_diag_a2 and f0_coh_a2: both 16. The auditor confirmed |eigenvalue|_min of I + A(Q4) is 1 (spectrum 5,3,1,-1,-3), so a float rank threshold cannot plausibly miss it. Cross-lane A2 agreement is therefore NOT evidence the jax float SVD path is sound.

f3_seam_satisfied_edges and f3_seam_total_edges: 32/32 forced, because a Q4 edge flips exactly one bit so r = low two bits either is unchanged or differs in one bit. The positive F3 check has no teeth here; R2 carries all of F3's discrimination.

f2_n2_degree_changed: true for any added edge whatsoever. It detects that an edge was added, not that the edge sits at Hamming distance 3. The distance-3 fact is computed by all three lanes but is not a contract key.
f2_n3_edge_counts_differ: edge count is a weak invariant; any two presentations with equal edge counts pass it unchallenged.
f3_r1_quotient_vertices: positive-only, 4, with no negative control, and all three lanes note the quotient EDGE count is unpinned (4 simple / 20 with loops / 32 with multiplicity).
SPUN: zero contract keys mention it. All three lanes measure it, nothing scores it, so a lane could omit SPUN entirely and satisfy the contract literally. Relabelling invariance is untested.

answers.can_this_estate_execute_finite_entropy_g: Correctly, yes, on this fixture: three engines and an independent stdlib re-derivation land on the same 21 values, and every hand ground truth holds. Independently, PARTLY. Value-correctness is independently carried three times over. Order-correctness is carried ZERO times by an engine lane and once by ground_truth_v0.py, which is a stdlib script, not an engine. A relabelled carrier passes all three engines silently.
answers.which_of_julia_jax_pytorch_genuinely_ran: All three, all at `passes local rerun`, none decorative. Julia 1.12.6 native (.jl executed by julia, Graphs.jl and Rational{BigInt} load-bearing, no python simulation). JAX 0.10.1 (svd and dot_general primitives in the jaxpr, 0 of 85 receipts numpy-typed). PyTorch 2.11.0 (45 distinct functions / 4324 dispatches at dispatch level, int64 Bareiss elimination). Each dies to exit 1 with 0 bytes when its engine is severed, and each moves its demanded numbers when its decisive kernel is mutated.
answers.which_fixtures_actually_DISCRIMINATED_ve: DISCRIMINATED: C1 dependency kill (all 3 lanes), C2a rank mutation (2/21 keys, all 3), C2b adjacency mutation (5/21 jax and pytorch, 2/21 julia), C3 integrity gates (pytorch and julia; jax does not enforce), C3 carrier sensitivity (14/21, all 3, including all 8 F0/F1 keys), C5 stale artifact for a different configuration or a tampered field (controller exit 3), C6b numpy attribution. MERELY COMPLETED: C4a and C4b wrong order (0/21 on every lane), C5 same-configuration stale artifact, C6 numpy poison as specified. Plus 7 of 21 contract keys that are carrier-invariant or forced and score nothing: both A0 keys, both A2 keys, both seam-edge keys, f2_n2_degree_changed, f2_n3_edge_counts_differ, f3_r1_quotient_vertices, and the entirely unscored SPUN presentation.
answers.is_it_justified_to_scale_formalize_furth: No, on all three, and the reasons are different for each. SCALE: no. Scaling a battery that cannot see permutation of its own carrier scales a blind spot; every added carrier inherits the same C4 hole. FORMALIZE FURTHER: no. Formalizing a 21-key contract in which 7 keys are forced and order is unscored would freeze the gap into the spec. CLOUD GPUs: no, and not for a correctness reason. The whole fixture is a 16-vertex hypercube; the slowest lane takes 5.8 s wall and is dominated by julia process startup, not arithmetic. A GPU would measure nothing this laptop has not already measured.
